script.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: “No warning shot, no second chance” presents the manager’s prior circumstances as known. The text does not say whether he received a warning or another chance.
“No shovel, no cup” suggests the manager lacks equipment. He says he is too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg.
“The day after the job ends” adds a specific time. The manager speaks of what will happen after his removal, without naming a day.
The text does not say the debtor walks away or establish what he owes afterward. It records what the manager tells him to write.
“Makes people glad to see him” states a reaction the text does not give. The manager wants people to welcome him, but their response is not reported.
“No shouting” asserts something the text does not say. It reports the master’s commendation without describing whether anyone shouted.
“The master lost money here” assumes an outcome the text does not report. It tells what the manager instructed the debtors to write.
The reference to the rich fool’s plan is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
“The welcome doesn't” run out goes beyond the text. Jesus calls the dwellings eternal; He does not say the welcome itself never ends.
The comparison about a dishonest cookie and box does not make sense: dishonesty is a person’s action, not a quality of a cookie.
“Leads to” makes dishonesty with little the cause of dishonesty with much. Jesus states that the person who is dishonest with little will also be dishonest with much.
“Worldly wealth comes first, and true riches come after” turns Jesus’ question into a stated sequence. The verse does not promise that sequence.
“Good memory” assumes the baker recognized and remembered the phrase from another passage, which has not been established.
“Faithfulness ... comes before getting something that's yours” turns Jesus’ question into a stated sequence and implies that faithfulness is followed by receiving possessions of one’s own.
